title: षष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 60 · Draupadi is dragged into the hall

summary.en: The usher sent to fetch Draupadi returns with her question: did Yudhishthira lose himself first, or her? Duryodhana sends Duhshasana, who drags her by the hair into the hall in her single garment during her period, while the elders sit silent and Bhima looks at Yudhishthira in fury.
summary.kn: ದ್ರೌಪದಿಯನ್ನು ಕರೆತರಲು ಹೋದ ಪ್ರಾತಿಕಾಮಿ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನು ಮೊದಲು ತನ್ನನ್ನು ಸೋತನೇ ಅವಳನ್ನೇ ಎಂಬ ಅವಳ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯೊಂದಿಗೆ ಮರಳುತ್ತಾನೆ. ದುರ್ಯೋಧನನು ದುಃಶಾಸನನನ್ನು ಕಳುಹಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ರಜಸ್ವಲೆಯಾಗಿ ಏಕವಸ್ತ್ರಳಾಗಿದ್ದ ಅವಳನ್ನು ಅವನು ಕೂದಲು ಹಿಡಿದು ಸಭೆಗೆ ಎಳೆತರುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಹಿರಿಯರು ಮೌನವಾಗಿರುತ್ತಾರೆ, ಭೀಮನು ಕೋಪದಿಂದ ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನನ್ನು ನೋಡುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: द्रौपदी को लाने भेजा गया प्रातिकामी उनके प्रश्न के साथ लौटता है: क्या युधिष्ठिर पहले स्वयं को हारे या उन्हें? दुर्योधन दुःशासन को भेजता है, जो रजस्वला और एकवस्त्रा द्रौपदी को बाल पकड़कर सभा में घसीट लाता है, जबकि वृद्ध मौन बैठे रहते हैं और भीम क्रोध से युधिष्ठिर को देखते हैं।
summary.te: ద్రౌపదిని తీసుకురావడానికి వెళ్లిన ప్రాతికామి, యుధిష్ఠిరుడు ముందు తనను ఓడాడా ఆమెను ఓడాడా అనే ఆమె ప్రశ్నతో తిరిగివస్తాడు. దుర్యోధనుడు దుశ్శాసనుని పంపుతాడు; రజస్వలగా ఏకవస్త్రగా ఉన్న ఆమెను అతడు జుట్టు పట్టి సభకు ఈడ్చుకొస్తాడు; పెద్దలు మౌనంగా ఉంటారు, భీముడు కోపంగా యుధిష్ఠిరుని చూస్తాడు.
summary.ta: திரௌபதியை அழைக்கச் சென்ற ப்ராதிகாமி, யுதிஷ்டிரர் முதலில் தம்மை இழந்தாரா அவளை இழந்தாரா என்ற அவள் கேள்வியுடன் திரும்புகிறான். துரியோதனன் துச்ஶாஸனனை அனுப்ப, மாதவிலக்கில் ஒற்றையாடையில் இருந்த அவளை அவன் கூந்தலைப் பற்றி ஸபைக்கு இழுத்து வருகிறான்; பெரியோர்கள் மௌனமாக இருக்க, பீமன் சினத்துடன் யுதிஷ்டிரரைப் பார்க்கிறான்.
summary.ml: ദ്രൗപദിയെ കൊണ്ടുവരാൻ അയച്ച ദൂതൻ ചോദ്യവുമായി മടങ്ങുന്നു: യുധിഷ്ഠിരൻ ആദ്യം തന്നെത്തന്നെയാണോ അതോ അവളെയാണോ നഷ്ടപ്പെടുത്തിയത്? ദുര്യോധനൻ ദുശ്ശാസനനെ അയയ്ക്കുന്നു; ആർത്തവകാലത്തായിരുന്ന ദ്രൗപദിയെ, ഒറ്റവസ്ത്രത്തിൽ മുടിക്ക് പിടിച്ചു വലിച്ച് അവൻ സഭയിലേക്ക് കൊണ്ടുവരുന്നു; മുതിർന്നവർ നിശ്ശബ്ദരായിരിക്കുമ്പോൾ ഭീമൻ കോപത്തോടെ യുധിഷ്ഠിരനെ നോക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 2.60; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Wed Apr 19 2006

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
धिगस्तु क्षत्तारमिति ब्रुवाणो
दर्पेण मत्तो धृतराष्ट्रस्य पुत्रः ।
अवैक्षत प्रातिकामीं सभाया-
मुवाच चैनं परमार्यमध्ये ॥

meaning.en: Saying Shame on Kshatta, Dhritarashtra's son, drunk with arrogance, looked at the charioteer Pratikamin in the assembly and spoke to him amid the noble men.

verses.text:
त्वं प्रातिकामिन्द्रौपदीमानयस्व
न ते भयं विद्यते पाण्डवेभ्यः ।
क्षत्ता ह्ययं विवदत्येव भीरु-
र्न चास्माकं वृद्धिकामः सदैव ॥

meaning.en: Pratikamin, go and bring Draupadi. You have nothing to fear from the Pandavas. This Kshatta is timid and keeps arguing; he does not always wish for our growth.

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः प्रातिकामी स सूतः
प्रायाच्छीघ्रं राजवचो निशम्य ।
प्रविश्य च श्वेव स सिंहगोष्ठं
समासदन्महिषीं पाण्डवानाम् ॥

meaning.en: Thus told, the charioteer Pratikamin, hearing the king's word, went quickly. Entering like a dog into a lion's den, he approached the Pandavas' queen.

verses.text: प्रातिकाम्युवाच

meaning.en: Pratikamin said:

verses.text:
युधिष्ठिरे द्यूतमदेन मत्ते
दुर्योधनो द्रौपदि त्वामजैषीत् ।
सा प्रपद्य त्वं धृतराष्ट्रस्य वेश्म
नयामि त्वां कर्मणे याज्ञसेनि ॥

meaning.en: Draupadi, since Yudhishthira is drunk with the passion for dice, Duryodhana has won you. Come now to Dhritarashtra's house; I will take you, daughter of Yajnasena, to work.

verses.text: द्रौपद्युवाच

meaning.en: Draupadi said:

verses.text:
कथं त्वेवं वदसि प्रातिकामि-
न्को वै दीव्येद्भार्यया राजपुत्रः ।
मूढो राजा द्यूतमदेन मत्त
आहो नान्यत्कैतवमस्य किंचित् ॥

meaning.en: Pratikamin, how can you say this? What prince would gamble his wife? Is the king deluded, drunk with dice, or did he have nothing else to stake?

verses.text: प्रातिकाम्युवाच

meaning.en: Pratikamin said:

verses.text:
यदा नाभूत्कैतवमन्यदस्य
तदादेवीत्पाण्डवोऽजातशत्रुः ।
न्यस्ताः पूर्वं भ्रातरस्तेन राज्ञा
स्वयं चात्मा त्वमथो राजपुत्रि ॥

meaning.en: When he had nothing else to stake, the Pandava born without an enemy played with you. First the king staked his brothers, then himself, and then you, princess.

verses.text: द्रौपद्युवाच

meaning.en: Draupadi said:

verses.text:
गच्छ त्वं कितवं गत्वा सभायां पृच्छ सूतज ।
किं नु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानं मां नु भारत ।
एतज्ज्ञात्वा त्वमागच्छ ततो मां नय सूतज ॥

meaning.en: Go, son of a charioteer, to the gambler in the assembly and ask: Did you lose yourself first, or me, Bharata? Learn that and come back; then take me, charioteer's son.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
सभां गत्वा स चोवाच द्रौपद्यास्तद्वचस्तदा ।
कस्येशो नः पराजैषीरिति त्वामाह द्रौपदी ।
किं नु पूर्वं पराजैषीरात्मानमथ वापि माम् ॥

meaning.en: He went to the hall and told Draupadi's words: Whose master were you when you lost us? Draupadi asks you this. Did you lose yourself first, or me?

verses.text:
युधिष्ठिरस्तु निश्चेष्टो गतसत्त्व इवाभवत् ।
न तं सूतं प्रत्युवाच वचनं साध्वसाधु वा ॥

meaning.en: But Yudhishthira stood motionless, as if lifeless, and answered the charioteer neither well nor ill.

verses.text: दुर्योधन उवाच

meaning.en: Duryodhana said:

verses.text:
इहैत्य कृष्णा पाञ्चाली प्रश्नमेतं प्रभाषताम् ।
इहैव सर्वे शृण्वन्तु तस्या अस्य च यद्वचः ॥

meaning.en: Let Panchali Krishna come here and put her question here. Let all hear what she says and what he says.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
स गत्वा राजभवनं दुर्योधनवशानुगः ।
उवाच द्रौपदीं सूतः प्रातिकामी व्यथन्निव ॥

meaning.en: Following Duryodhana's command, the charioteer went to the royal quarters, and as if pained said to Draupadi:

verses.text:
सभ्यास्त्वमी राजपुत्र्याह्वयन्ति
मन्ये प्राप्तः संक्षयः कौरवाणाम् ।
न वै समृद्धिं पालयते लघीया-
न्यत्त्वं सभामेष्यसि राजपुत्रि ॥

meaning.en: The assembly members summon you, princess. I think the end of the Kauravas has come. A weak king cannot protect prosperity when you, princess, must come to the hall.

verses.text: द्रौपद्युवाच

meaning.en: Draupadi said:

verses.text:
एवं नूनं व्यदधात्संविधाता
स्पर्शावुभौ स्पृशतो धीरबालौ ।
धर्मं त्वेकं परमं प्राह लोके
स नः शमं धास्यति गोप्यमानः ॥

meaning.en: Surely the Ordainer has so arranged; both the wise and the childish feel the same two touches. Dharma alone is said to be highest in the world; if guarded, it will bring us peace.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
युधिष्ठिरस्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा दुर्योधनचिकीर्षितम् ।
द्रौपद्याः संमतं दूतं प्राहिणोद्भरतर्षभ ॥

meaning.en: Hearing what Duryodhana intended, Yudhishthira, bull of the Bharatas, sent a messenger who was accepted by Draupadi.

verses.text:
एकवस्त्रा अधोनीवी रोदमाना रजस्वला ।
सभामागम्य पाञ्चाली श्वशुरस्याग्रतोऽभवत् ॥

meaning.en: In a single garment, with its waist-knot loose, weeping and in her season, Panchali came into the hall and stood before her father-in-law.

verses.text:
ततस्तेषां मुखमालोक्य राजा
दुर्योधनः सूतमुवाच हृष्टः ।
इहैवैतामानय प्रातिकामि-
न्प्रत्यक्षमस्याः कुरवो ब्रुवन्तु ॥

meaning.en: Then King Duryodhana, looking at their faces, said happily to the charioteer: Pratikamin, bring her right here, and let the Kurus speak before her eyes.

verses.text:
ततः सूतस्तस्य वशानुगामी
भीतश्च कोपाद्द्रुपदात्मजायाः ।
विहाय मानं पुनरेव सभ्या-
नुवाच कृष्णां किमहं ब्रवीमि ॥

meaning.en: Then the charioteer, under his sway but afraid of the anger of Drupada's daughter, put aside his pride and said again to the assembly, What shall I tell Krishna?

verses.text: दुर्योधन उवाच

meaning.en: Duryodhana said:

verses.text:
दुःशासनैष मम सूतपुत्रो
वृकोदरादुद्विजतेऽल्पचेताः ।
स्वयं प्रगृह्यानय याज्ञसेनीं
किं ते करिष्यन्त्यवशाः सपत्नाः ॥

meaning.en: Duhshasana, this charioteer's son is shy and small-minded, afraid of Vrikodara. Take Yajnasena's daughter yourself and bring her; what will powerless rivals do to you?

verses.text:
ततः समुत्थाय स राजपुत्रः
श्रुत्वा भ्रातुः कोपविरक्तदृष्टिः ।
प्रविश्य तद्वेश्म महारथाना-
मित्यब्रवीद्द्रौपदीं राजपुत्रीम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the prince rose, his eyes reddened with anger at his brother's words, and entering the mansion of the great warriors said to the princess Draupadi:

verses.text:
एह्येहि पाञ्चालि जितासि कृष्णे
दुर्योधनं पश्य विमुक्तलज्जा ।
कुरून्भजस्वायतपद्मनेत्रे
धर्मेण लब्धासि सभां परैहि ॥

meaning.en: Come, come, Panchali; you are won, Krishna. Look at Duryodhana, giving up shame. Serve the Kurus, lotus-eyed one; you were won by right. Come to the hall.

verses.text:
ततः समुत्थाय सुदुर्मनाः सा
विवर्णमामृज्य मुखं करेण ।
आर्ता प्रदुद्राव यतः स्त्रियस्ता
वृद्धस्य राज्ञः कुरुपुंगवस्य ॥

meaning.en: Then, greatly distressed, she rose, wiped her pale face with her hand, and in anguish ran to where the women of the aged Kuru king were.

verses.text:
ततो जवेनाभिससार रोषा-
द्दुःशासनस्तामभिगर्जमानः ।
दीर्घेषु नीलेष्वथ चोर्मिमत्सु
जग्राह केशेषु नरेन्द्रपत्नीम् ॥

meaning.en: Then Duhshasana raced after her in rage, roaring, and seized the king's wife by her long, dark, wavy hair.

verses.text:
ये राजसूयावभृथे जलेन
महाक्रतौ मन्त्रपूतेन सिक्ताः ।
ते पाण्डवानां परिभूय वीर्यं
बलात्प्रमृष्टा धृतराष्ट्रजेन ॥

meaning.en: The hair that was sprinkled with mantra-purified water at the great Rajasuya, at the concluding bath, was roughly handled by Dhritarashtra's son, slighting the Pandavas' might.

verses.text:
स तां परामृश्य सभासमीप-
मानीय कृष्णामतिकृष्णकेशीम् ।
दुःशासनो नाथवतीमनाथव-
च्चकर्ष वायुः कदलीमिवार्ताम् ॥

meaning.en: Seizing her, Duhshasana brought Krishna, dark-haired, to the near side of the assembly. Though she had protectors, he dragged her like one without, as wind drags a plantain tree in distress.

verses.text:
सा कृष्यमाणा नमिताङ्गयष्टिः
शनैरुवाचाद्य रजस्वलास्मि ।
एकं च वासो मम मन्दबुद्धे
सभां नेतुं नार्हसि मामनार्य ॥

meaning.en: As she was dragged, her slender body bent, she said softly, Today I am in my season, fool; I have just one garment. Ignoble man, you must not take me to the hall.

verses.text:
ततोऽब्रवीत्तां प्रसभं निगृह्य
केशेषु कृष्णेषु तदा स कृष्णाम् ।
कृष्णं च जिष्णुं च हरिं नरं च
त्राणाय विक्रोश नयामि हि त्वाम् ॥

meaning.en: Then, forcibly holding her by her dark hair, he said to Krishna: Cry out for Krishna, Jishnu, Hari and Nara to save you; I will take you anyway.

verses.text:
रजस्वला वा भव याज्ञसेनि
एकाम्बरा वाप्यथ वा विवस्त्रा ।
द्यूते जिता चासि कृतासि दासी
दासीषु कामश्च यथोपजोषम् ॥

meaning.en: Be in your season, Yajnasena's daughter, or in one garment, or without clothes; you were won at dice and made a slave, and one may take pleasure with slave women as one likes.

verses.text:
प्रकीर्णकेशी पतितार्धवस्त्रा
दुःशासनेन व्यवधूयमाना ।
ह्रीमत्यमर्षेण च दह्यमाना
शनैरिदं वाक्यमुवाच कृष्णा ॥

meaning.en: With hair loose, half her garment fallen, shaken by Duhshasana, shamed and burning with indignation, Krishna said softly:

verses.text:
इमे सभायामुपदिष्टशास्त्राः
क्रियावन्तः सर्व एवेन्द्रकल्पाः ।
गुरुस्थाना गुरवश्चैव सर्वे
तेषामग्रे नोत्सहे स्थातुमेवम् ॥

meaning.en: These in the assembly are learned in the scriptures, men of rites, all like Indra, elders and teachers. I cannot bear to stand before them like this.

verses.text:
नृशंसकर्मंस्त्वमनार्यवृत्त
मा मां विवस्त्रां कृधि मा विकार्षीः ।
न मर्षयेयुस्तव राजपुत्राः
सेन्द्रापि देवा यदि ते सहायाः ॥

meaning.en: Cruel doer, man of ignoble conduct, do not make me naked, do not drag me. The princes would not forgive you, even if Indra and the gods were your helpers.

verses.text:
धर्मे स्थितो धर्मसुतश्च राजा
धर्मश्च सूक्ष्मो निपुणोपलभ्यः ।
वाचापि भर्तुः परमाणुमात्रं
नेच्छामि दोषं स्वगुणान्विसृज्य ॥

meaning.en: The king, son of Dharma, stands in dharma, and dharma is subtle and understood by the skilled. Even in speech I do not wish the smallest atom of fault in my husband, leaving aside my own merits.

verses.text:
इदं त्वनार्यं कुरुवीरमध्ये
रजस्वलां यत्परिकर्षसे माम् ।
न चापि कश्चित्कुरुतेऽत्र पूजां
ध्रुवं तवेदं मतमन्वपद्यन् ॥

meaning.en: It is ignoble that in the midst of the Kuru heroes you drag me, in my season. And no one here shows regard; surely they approve your intent.

verses.text:
धिगस्तु नष्टः खलु भारतानां
धर्मस्तथा क्षत्रविदां च वृत्तम् ।
यत्राभ्यतीतां कुरुधर्मवेलां
प्रेक्षन्ति सर्वे कुरवः सभायाम् ॥

meaning.en: Shame! Surely the dharma of the Bharatas is lost, and the conduct of those who know the kshatriya way, when all the Kurus in the assembly watch the Kuru law's boundary crossed.

verses.text:
द्रोणस्य भीष्मस्य च नास्ति सत्त्वं
ध्रुवं तथैवास्य महात्मनोऽपि ।
राज्ञस्तथा हीममधर्ममुग्रं
न लक्षयन्ते कुरुवृद्धमुख्याः ॥

meaning.en: Drona and Bhishma have no strength, and neither has this great-souled king; the Kuru elders do not notice this fierce wrong.

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवन्ती करुणं सुमध्यमा
काक्षेण भर्तॄन्कुपितानपश्यत् ।
सा पाण्डवान्कोपपरीतदेहा-
न्संदीपयामास कटाक्षपातैः ॥

meaning.en: Speaking so piteously, the slender-waisted woman looked sideways at her angry husbands. With her glances she kindled the Pandavas, whose bodies were filled with wrath.

verses.text:
हृतेन राज्येन तथा धनेन
रत्नैश्च मुख्यैर्न तथा बभूव ।
यथार्तया कोपसमीरितेन
कृष्णाकटाक्षेण बभूव दुःखम् ॥

meaning.en: Not even the loss of their kingdom, wealth and finest jewels hurt them as did Krishna's sidelong look, afflicted and moved by anger.

verses.text:
दुःशासनश्चापि समीक्ष्य कृष्णा-
मवेक्षमाणां कृपणान्पतींस्तान् ।
आधूय वेगेन विसंज्ञकल्पा-
मुवाच दासीति हसन्निवोग्रः ॥

meaning.en: Duhshasana, seeing Krishna looking at her wretched husbands, shook her violently, as if she were senseless, and said fiercely, laughing, Slave!

verses.text:
कर्णस्तु तद्वाक्यमतीव हृष्टः
संपूजयामास हसन्सशब्दम् ।
गान्धारराजः सुबलस्य पुत्र-
स्तथैव दुःशासनमभ्यनन्दत् ॥

meaning.en: Karna, greatly pleased with those words, praised them with loud laughter, and the king of Gandhara, son of Subala, likewise applauded Duhshasana.

verses.text:
सभ्यास्तु ये तत्र बभूवुरन्ये
ताभ्यामृते धार्तराष्ट्रेण चैव ।
तेषामभूद्दुःखमतीव कृष्णां
दृष्ट्वा सभायां परिकृष्यमाणाम् ॥

meaning.en: But among the other assembly members, except those two and Dhritarashtra's son, there was great pain at seeing Krishna dragged in the hall.

verses.text: भीष्म उवाच

meaning.en: Bhishma said:

verses.text:
न धर्मसौक्ष्म्यात्सुभगे विवक्तुं
शक्नोमि ते प्रश्नमिमं यथावत् ।
अस्वो ह्यशक्तः पणितुं परस्वं
स्त्रियश्च भर्तुर्वशतां समीक्ष्य ॥

meaning.en: Fortunate lady, from the subtlety of dharma I cannot answer your question properly. One who has nothing cannot stake another's property, but a wife is seen to be under her husband's power.

verses.text:
त्यजेत सर्वां पृथिवीं समृद्धां
युधिष्ठिरः सत्यमथो न जह्यात् ।
उक्तं जितोऽस्मीति च पाण्डवेन
तस्मान्न शक्नोमि विवेक्तुमेतत् ॥

meaning.en: Yudhishthira might give up the whole prosperous earth but would not abandon truth. The Pandava said, I am won; so I cannot decide this.

verses.text:
द्यूतेऽद्वितीयः शकुनिर्नरेषु
कुन्तीसुतस्तेन निसृष्टकामः ।
न मन्यते तां निकृतिं महात्मा
तस्मान्न ते प्रश्नमिमं ब्रवीमि ॥

meaning.en: Shakuni has no equal at dice among men, and the son of Kunti played of his own accord. The great-souled one does not regard that as a trick; so I cannot answer your question.

verses.text: द्रौपद्युवाच

meaning.en: Draupadi said:

verses.text:
आहूय राजा कुशलैः सभायां
दुष्टात्मभिर्नैकृतिकैरनार्यैः ।
द्यूतप्रियैर्नातिकृतप्रयत्नः
कस्मादयं नाम निसृष्टकामः ॥

meaning.en: The king was summoned to the hall by skilled, evil-minded, ignoble cheats who love dice, though he was not an expert; why then did he play of his own free will?

verses.text:
स शुद्धभावो निकृतिप्रवृत्ति-
मबुध्यमानः कुरुपाण्डवाग्र्यः ।
संभूय सर्वैश्च जितोऽपि यस्मा-
त्पश्चाच्च यत्कैतवमभ्युपेतः ॥

meaning.en: That pure-hearted best of the Kurus and Pandavas, not knowing their tricks, was beaten by all of them in concert, and then afterwards took to gambling.

verses.text:
तिष्ठन्ति चेमे कुरवः सभाया-
मीशाः सुतानां च तथा स्नुषाणाम् ।
समीक्ष्य सर्वे मम चापि वाक्यं
विब्रूत मे प्रश्नमिमं यथावत् ॥

meaning.en: These Kurus stand in the assembly, lords over their sons and daughters-in-law. All of you, considering my word as well, answer my question properly.

verses.text: वैशंपायन उवाच

meaning.en: Vaishampayana said:

verses.text:
तथा ब्रुवन्तीं करुणं रुदन्ती-
मवेक्षमाणामसकृत्पतींस्तान् ।
दुःशासनः परुषाण्यप्रियाणि
वाक्यान्युवाचामधुराणि चैव ॥

meaning.en: As she spoke so piteously, weeping, again and again looking at her husbands, Duhshasana said harsh, unkind and unpleasant words to her.

verses.text:
तां कृष्यमाणां च रजस्वलां च
स्रस्तोत्तरीयामतदर्हमाणाम् ।
वृकोदरः प्रेक्ष्य युधिष्ठिरं च
चकार कोपं परमार्तरूपः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing her dragged, in her season, with her upper garment slipping, undeserving of this, Vrikodara looked at Yudhishthira and became very angry, in great distress.
